how.title: How it works
how.0.title: Stockfish finds ALL your blunders
how.0.body: Yes, even the ones you played on the toilet.
how.1.title: Train a few every day
how.1.body: Each blunder comes back on a four-rep ladder over about a month. A few minutes a day keeps the pattern mastered for your next game.
how.2.title: Repeat until the answer is automatic
how.2.body: Blunders happen from time trouble and blind spots. The best move has to be automatic in order to find it under pressure.
how.3.title: Keep the streak
how.3.body: Play a game, train your positions, come back tomorrow. Your streak, the weekly board and email reminders keep you honest to your goals.
ladder.title: The four-rep ladder
ladder.subtitle: One pattern · same position · drilled until it's yours
ladder.0.headline: You blunder
ladder.0.body: First encounter. Stockfish shows the move you missed — it stings, you log it, you move on.
ladder.1.headline: You're seeing it
ladder.1.body: A few days in. The shape is familiar; the right move starts to surface before you finish reading the position.
ladder.2.headline: Locked in
ladder.2.body: A month later, the pattern is automatic — and you spot it across the board, in your own games, without thinking.
ladder.footer: Every blunder climbs the same four-rung ladder — then returns every {days} days to stay sharp.
ladder.firstTry: Every first-try solve moves it up one rung.
why.title: Why you're stuck
why.0.title: Learning needs friction
why.0.body: To improve, your brain has to struggle with the same idea — many times over. Most chess training skips this. Blitz while half-watching TV trains nothing. Puzzles fade within a day of solving them.{c1} Patterns stick when you face the same position on different days until the answer is automatic.{c2}{c3}
why.1.title: Blunders decide your games
why.1.body: Most games below 2000 Elo are decided by one player handing the other a winning position. I've coached adult improvers for years and climbed to 2300+ on chess.com myself, and I see the same thing every time: one missed move decides the game. That's what you need to drill.
why.2.title: Drill the games you actually played
why.2.body: The patterns that keep beating you are sitting in your own losses. PatternChess pulls your games from Chess.com or Lichess, runs Stockfish over them, and collects the moves where you actually lost ground into one structured set. It's the same repeat-until-automatic idea Tikkanen used on his way to three GM norms in seven weeks.{c4}
why.3.title: Consistency compounds
why.3.body: Ten minutes today does more than two hours next Sunday. Spaced practice works because it gives you time to digest new chess patterns.{c3} The hard part is showing up, so we made it easy: a daily plan, a streak, and reminders to keep you consistent.
about.title: Why I built this
about.p1: I built PatternChess because I wanted to test an insight I had from my own training. I started studying chess seriously as an adult, and the only method that got me results was spaced repetition. I'd print out a set of puzzles and review them every night until I could solve a set of 200-300 puzzles in one sitting.
about.p2: The issue was, these positions taught me how to win. They didn't teach me how to stop losing. Without an expensive coach, no one could tell me exactly where my blind spots were, and I had no way of training the exact positions I was losing in. As a professional software engineer, I thought I might finally be able to come up with a solution. So I built one.
